analysis.title: TMT Today - 30 Oct 2026 (Leyla Kamshad, GS Global Banking & Markets, FICC & Equities TMT Trading)
key_insights: Futures sharply lower (Nasdaq -250bps, S&P -110bps, Russell -50bps) as another batch of disappointing tech earnings weighs on Tech/AI sentiment. Cash equities in the macro section show NDX -2.40%, SPX -1.00%, RTY -60bps.

INTC is -25% pre-market. Q3 revenue was $16.5bn (GS $17.0bn, Street $16.4bn). Non-GAAP EPS was $0.52 (GS $0.47, Street $0.39). Q4 guide midpoint is revenue $15.5bn (GS $18.0bn, Street $17.0bn), gross margin 38% (Street 42.5%) and EPS $0.25 (Street $0.43). DELL and HPQ are lower in sympathy.

INTC datacenter (DCAI) revenue was $7.3bn, +17% QoQ and +78% YoY, and the company expects mid-teens sequential DCAI growth in Q4 while capacity constrained. It sees server CPU units growing over 30% in 2026 and 2027 and a ~$200bn TAM by 2030, driven by agentic AI.

INTC management sees a PC market weaker into 2027. It expects 2026 PC units down ~12% and a ~10% TAM decline in 2027, with Q4 client revenue down ~20% QoQ and the inventory correction extending through 1Q and possibly 2Q. Causes cited are limited IT budgets, elevated inventories and memory constraints.

AMZN is -7% pre-market. AWS revenue beat Street/GSe, but 39% growth was below buyside expectations and incremental margins decelerated 8pts QoQ. Q3 advertising was ~4-6% below GSe/Street on a ~850bps Prime Day/NBA timing headwind, and Q4 operating income guide was ~3-6% below at the midpoint. Positives: AWS capacity largely sold out for 2 years, management projects AWS growth of +40% in 2027 and 2028, and a path to a $1tn annual revenue run rate.

SNDK is -7 to -8% pre-market despite a beat and a Q4 guide above Street (revenue $12.4bn midpoint vs Street $12.08bn, EPS midpoint $56.00 vs Street $52.94). MU is lower in sympathy. Datacenter is now about half of industry NAND bit demand, KV cache is expected to be ~35% of the AI datacenter market by 2030, and an 8:1 stock split is effective November 20, 2026.

Kioxia guided quarterly operating profit of ¥2 trillion vs estimates of ¥2.35 trillion. NAND ASP rose a mid-20% in the three months to September vs 70% in the prior quarter, signaling flash price increases are leveling off. This is a negative data point for memory and semis.

RDDT is -20% pre-market. US DAUs declined sequentially, search referral traffic declines accelerated through Q3 and continued into early Q4, and a low-double-digit % decline in total DAUq is possible in Q4. Ad revenue grew +54% YoY. The company plans to limit third-party data access.

TWLO is -17 to -18% pre-market despite a beat and raise. Organic revenue growth slowed 100bps QoQ to 16%, DBNR fell 200bps QoQ to 114%, and Q4 guidance was soft. Initial 2027 guidance is >10% organic growth and EBIT/FCF of at least $1.35bn.

RBLX is -17% pre-market. Q3 bookings beat, but Q4 bookings guidance implies a 10-15% YoY decline and Q4 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $320-380mm is well below Street, on higher AI infrastructure spend and O18 marketing. Q3 DAUs/hours were down 9%/15% YoY.

Crude is bid (WTI +2%) after reports of a tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz and renewed Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran for deal talks, and a US resumption of strikes on Iran after next week's midterms remains in play.

Binance estimates a $6.3bn hack, the largest in crypto, and suspended withdrawals Friday. About $3bn of assets were frozen on-chain, Binance pledged to cover all losses, and withdrawals are expected to resume by Sunday.

MediaTek guided Q4 revenue to NT$210.1-221.8bn (at least +40%), with the midpoint above the NT$210.6bn consensus. It expects custom AI chip sales of about $16bn in 2027 and an operating margin above 20% in 2027.

INGM Q3 EPS was $0.91 vs GSe $0.82 and consensus $0.78, with revenue of $15.2bn vs GSe $14.0bn. AI deal revenue was $1.8bn vs $700mn a year ago. Q4 guide is +19% revenue growth at the midpoint including an extra-week benefit.
PINS Q3 results and Q4 guide came in below expectations on European headwinds from EU de-minimis rules. MAUs hit a record 661mm.
SIRI raised all 2026 guidance by $25M: revenue ~$8.55B, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.65B and FCF ~$1.40B. Self-pay net adds are now expected ~flat vs 2025.
Spotify is targeting a Q1 2027 launch of an AI remix service, possibly priced at an extra $4-5 a month, subject to licensing deals (FT).

sector_views.rationale: The note describes tech earnings as disappointing and deflating sentiment across Tech/AI, but states no formal sector stance.

earnings_insights: INTC Q3 (reported, non-GAAP): revenue $16.5bn vs GS $17.0bn / Street $16.4bn, gross margin 44.1% vs Street 41.9%, operating margin 19.6% vs Street 16.5%, EPS $0.52 vs GS $0.47 / Street $0.39. CCG revenue $8.1bn (Street $8.9bn), DCAI $7.3bn (Street $6.6bn), Foundry $6.7bn (Street $6.0bn). Q4 guide midpoint (estimate): revenue $15.5bn vs Street $17.0bn, non-GAAP gross margin 38% vs Street 42.5%, non-GAAP EPS $0.25 vs Street $0.43.

SNDK FQ1'27 (reported): revenue $11.03bn vs GS $11.22bn / Street (Visible Alpha) $10.74bn, gross margin 85.1%, non-GAAP EPS $49.51 vs GS $49.80 / Street $46.73. Q4 guide midpoint: revenue $12.4bn (GS $13.55bn, Street $12.08bn), gross margin 85.0%, non-GAAP EPS $56.00 (GS $59.71, Street $52.94). Buybacks total $9.5bn with $10.5bn authorization remaining. Ten long-term supply agreements with 8 customers.

AMZN Q3 (reported): AWS revenue beat Street/GSe with 39% growth, below buyside expectations. Advertising ~4-6% below GSe/Street. Q4 operating income guide ~3-6% below GSe/Street at the midpoint. Management expects high-teens ad growth in Q4.
RDDT Q3 (reported): revenue beat GSe/Street and guidance, ad revenue +54% YoY, US DAUs declined sequentially. Q4 outlook weak, with a possible low-double-digit % decline in total DAUq.

TWLO Q3 (reported): revenue 3% above FactSet consensus, 2026 revenue guidance raised 175bps, 2026 EBIT guidance raised 5%, organic growth 16%, gross profit growth 18%, DBNR 114% (110% excluding carrier fees). Initial 2027 guide: >10% organic growth, EBIT/FCF of at least $1.35bn.
RBLX Q3'26 (reported): bookings ahead of GSe/Street. Q4'26 bookings guide implies a 10-15% YoY decline, and Q4'26 adjusted EBITDA guide $320-380mm is below GSe/Street.

INGM 3Q26 (reported): EPS $0.91 vs GSe $0.82 / consensus (FactSet) $0.78, revenue $15.2bn vs GSe $14.0bn / consensus $13.8bn, gross margin 6.5%, EBIT margin 2.1%. 4Q26 guide: +19% revenue at the midpoint, including an extra week (GSe ~8.5pt benefit). 2027 outlook reaffirmed at LSD% revenue growth.
PINS Q3'26 (reported): results and Q4 guide below expectations on European headwinds. Record MAUs of 661mm.

SIRI 3Q26 (reported): mostly in line to slightly better vs Visible Alpha consensus. 2026 guidance raised by $25M each: revenue ~$8.55B, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.65B, FCF ~$1.40B. GS estimates ~299k self-pay net losses in FY26.
Kioxia (reported guidance): quarterly operating profit outlook ¥2 trillion vs estimate ¥2.35 trillion.
MediaTek (guidance): Q4 revenue NT$210.1-221.8bn vs average analyst estimate NT$210.6bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Crude is bid on a reported tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure, adding a supply-risk premium.
Pre-market futures move reflecting disappointing tech earnings.
Broad equity futures weaker, led by tech.
Small caps fall less than large-cap tech.

crypto_views: Binance estimates a $6.3bn hack, the largest in crypto history. Withdrawals were suspended Friday, about $3bn was frozen on blockchain networks, and Binance pledged to cover all losses.
Co-founder Yi He said withdrawals were expected to resume by Sunday. Bloomberg links the incident to growing concern about hacker risk in the age of AI.
risk_factors: Further disappointing tech earnings could deepen the deflation of Tech/AI sentiment.
Memory price increases are leveling off per Kioxia, and high memory prices are hurting PC demand per INTC.
Possible resumption of US strikes on Iran after the midterms, plus Hormuz and Red Sea disruption to energy supply.
Capex-driven FCF headwinds at AMZN remain an overhang.
Search referral traffic declines hurt RDDT user growth.
Binance's $6.3bn hack and the security risk it signals for crypto platforms.
vol_and_positioning: Most active high-touch names: GOOG/L, INTC, AMZN, NOW, AMAT, HPQ, NFLX, T, TMUS.
geopolitical: Reported tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz and renewed Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure.
Qatari mediators returned to Tehran for deal talks coordinated with Washington (Reuters).
Signs that the US may resume strikes on Iran after midterms next week remain in play.

tension_points.bull_case: INTC DCAI grew 78% YoY with server CPU units expected up over 30% in 2026 and 2027. AMZN says AWS capacity is largely sold out for 2 years with +40% growth projected for 2027 and 2028. SNDK guided Q4 above Street on datacenter NAND demand and long-term supply agreements.
tension_points.bear_case: INTC sees PC units down ~12% in 2026 and a ~10% TAM decline in 2027, and cut Q4 guidance well below Street. Kioxia says NAND price increases are leveling off, and AMZN's AWS growth of 39% missed buyside expectations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further memory-price slowdown or additional AI-related guidance misses like Kioxia's would undercut the AI datacenter bull case.
